## The Observer Pattern and B-Trees: A Detailed Examination

The observer pattern and B-trees are two foundational concepts in computer science, but they solve very different problems. The observer pattern is a behavioral software design pattern that enables objects to communicate in a decoupled, event-driven manner. B-trees are self-balancing tree data structures designed for efficient storage and retrieval of sorted data, especially on disk-based systems. Understanding how each works, their complexity characteristics, and when to choose them over alternatives is essential for designing robust software systems.
